speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Rather than a "democracy of words" – mere political rhetoric or adversarial debate.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Fifty-five years on, this concept of a "democracy of deeds" remains deeply relevant.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Indeed, a "we first" society which the Prime Minister has rallied us towards, is a society where the democracy of deeds flourishes.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Through several initiatives, we have observed the democracy of deeds manifest in three ways.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, residents taking the responsibility to act and solve problems.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Second, residents having the imagination to create shared spaces.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Third, residents demonstrating the maturity to reach consensus through dialogue.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In August last year, a group of residents of Seng Poh estate in Tiong Bahru led by Mr Kelvin Ang wrote to me.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They had observed a worsening issue of the blue recycling bins in their estate being contaminated and becoming littering spots which spoilt the environment of their beautiful neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They sought my support to try a different approach.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Remove the blue bins and they would organise regular recycling collection drives instead to ensure that residents sorted and deposited clean recyclables.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, I contacted the National Environment Agency (NEA) to give my support for the initiative and requested that they partner us too.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What heartened me most was that our residents were stepping forth to take on responsibility for a shared problem and that NEA was prepared to cede some level of control and test a different approach with us.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Today, the "Bye Bye Blue Bins" pilot in Seng Poh estate is ongoing.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We have removed the bins for three weeks and have conducted two recycling collection drives.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The residents who proposed the initiative have worked incredibly hard, not just to organise the recycling collection events, but to knock on doors, put up and distribute flyers all over the estate so that fellow residents know about the initiative and have avenues to provide feedback.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They have also been working closely with the Town Council to coordinate enforcement.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While the early results have been encouraging, it is early days yet.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The team is collecting feedback and will continue to improve the approach.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In December last year, another resident, also from Seng Poh estate, Mr Warren Wee, wrote to me as well.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: He is an art curator and wanted to organise a digital art exhibition at the Tiong Bahru Air Raid Shelter where he would invite both local and international artists to present their works.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: His exhibition ran for a week from 19 to 26 January this year and I visited it three times: the first at his invitation for the opening reception, but the latter two were my own accord to bring the media and friends because I thought it was an excellent exhibition and I was very proud to share what our local boy had achieved.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Shin Min ran an article about the exhibition, spotlighting an artificial intelligence (AI) work by Ms Bianca Tse from Hong Kong, which seeks to recreate the Kowloon Walled City.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: She told me that the setting of the Tiong Bahru Air Raid Shelter captured the emotions she wanted to evoke through the work of the Walled City.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Both were harsh environments which yet sheltered resilient communities.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Anyone who has visited the Air Raid Shelter will know what she means.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It has been largely untouched since the 1940s.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There are areas which are leaking and there are broken bricks in some places.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Yet, Warren had the determination and boldness to conceptualise a digital art exhibition in the Shelter.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: He brought in works, like Bianca's, which spoke to the natural conditions of the Shelter and put in quite significant resources himself to ensure that it would be fit and safe for the public to spend some time in.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Warren told me he was fascinated by the space since he was young: its heritage, its history, how it would have held more than 1,600 residents during the Second World War.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: He asked if it would be possible for the Government to retrofit it basically, for better ventilation and environment, and his dream will be to run it as a more permanent art museum and heritage node.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They sell their ideas to their fellow residents, the ideas are put to a vote and those that fall within the budget get implemented.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, ideas from residents, voted by residents, built for residents.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: When IPS approached me with the concept last year, I was enthusiastic to pilot it.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Because I strongly believe in the potential of such a project in strengthening the sense of ownership and belonging of our residents and that given the right resources and facilitation, our residents will be able to develop the best ideas for their neighbourhoods.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We completed the kick-off session for the pilot two weeks ago.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Since then, IPS has worked with the residents to categorise the ideas into seven areas.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They conducted a deep dive with 25 residents last weekend.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Residents volunteered to lead the work, set out detailed proposals based on the ideas in collaboration with the other residents.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These residents will be hard at work over the next couple of weeks.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Then, the ideas will be put to a feasibility committee made up of the technical agencies before we proceed with an exhibition and voting.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Residents from other estates in the division have written to me, volunteering to lead similar "Bye Bye Blue Bins" initiatives in their own estates.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Other have asked when can they introduce PB in their estates as well.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is my hope and belief that some of these pilots we are conducting here can be scaled up to other parts of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But let me share some early reflections on the role of the Government, citizens and the Member of Parliament in making the transition.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In fact, another of my residents, Ms Diana Lau, from Boon Tiong estate applied herself for the Lively Places Fund and led the painting of a beautiful community street mural at Eng Hoon Street, turning what was a relatively underutilised pedestrianised street into a vibrant community hub and Instagrammable location.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, my sense is that these initiatives are positioned to run alongside the Government's infrastructure and planning approach.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They are "good to have" micro-activations of public spaces which otherwise do not interact with or influence the core of the Government's plans and policies.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But to build a democracy of deeds, I believe we should go much further and deeper, to place citizenship engagement right at the heart of our infrastructure and planning approach, in shaping our communities and our neighbourhoods.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Currently, the Singapore Land Authority (SLA) tenders out such properties using the price-quality system when they want the properties to be managed in ways that address other objectives, such as heritage rejuvenation.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This has led to high-quality lifestyle hubs, such as New Bahru and Kada, which require professionalised operations and commercial viability to run.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: One where the Government invites ground-up proposals for state properties – proposals which produce social impact.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It can be a community hub for youths or a heritage living space, perhaps, even a creative arts museum, like what my resident Warren envisaged for the Tiong Bahru Air Raid Shelter.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Under this model, we may see more social enterprises and ground-up collectives being awarded the use of such properties.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Imagine the energy that will be brought to our neighbourhoods if just a segment of them are converted to such community regeneration stations.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Second, how we conduct Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP).

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am very glad that HDB agreed to partner us for the PB in Spottiswoode Park.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I see this as the first step in seeing how we can potentially incorporate such a process into NRP.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We scheduled the PB pilot to run alongside the NRP process in Spottiswoode Park, so that all the implementing agencies, as well as our residents can experience how these can work side by side, and the difference in their level of engagement and their appetite for each of them.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Third, how we conduct recycling and other sustainability initiatives.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am similarly heartened that NEA and CORA, the recycling operator, also agreed to partner us for our "Bye Bye Blue Bins" pilot.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This boldness to try out something different is refreshing and invigorating for residents who are prepared to step up.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Instead of a one-size fits all approach, where waste is centrally collected and recycling contamination relatively high, a localised recycling approach may be much more effective in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am sure there are several other areas.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many, if not all of our Government agencies have a key role to play.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, for it to happen, I believe we need MCCY to lead the whole-of-Government charge in three key areas.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We need to set out a clear ambition – to go beyond funding, to deeply involved partnerships, where the agencies work closely with residents to design and activate their neighbourhoods.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We need strong coordination to ensure that the ambition permeates the whole-of-Government to develop a coherent agenda and programme which residents can refer to and see where they want to contribute.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We need public officers skilled at facilitating such partnerships with citizens.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: MCCY has been building this up through the SG Partnerships Office (SGPO), but we will need much more investment.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: MCCY can also work with partners, such as IPS to build a wider pool of skilled, not-for-profit, community-based facilitators.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As each of the initiatives I have highlighted show, the citizens have a very involved, time and effort intensive.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is not days, but weeks and months of effort.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is not raising suggestions, but detailing solutions, assessing trade-offs, convincing fellow citizens.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is not "I" versus the Government, or "I" versus my neighbour, but "we" – all together.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For every resident in Tanjong Pagar-Tiong Bahru who has participated in each of the initiatives, I thank you from the bottom of my heart.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It does not matter if the proposal came from my resident.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With a great number of residents involved, much more could have gone.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It starts with trust and ends with action.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Democracy of deeds is a simple yet powerful idea – that a thriving society is built not just by its government, but by everyone who lives in it through acts of participation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: This is precisely what we in government believe Singapore needs more of.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: A strong Singapore requires both sides to show up.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We need a society that sees shaping our shared future as something worth giving time and effort to.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: And we need a government that meets that energy with equal seriousness, building structures and a culture to make genuine partnership possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: People are already showing up – as we have seen from Mr Foo's examples – and we want to encourage them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We are on a journey to learn how to step back so that citizens step forward to issues that matter to them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The first is how citizens participate in shaping Government's plans and policies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: This calls for openness from Government to share trade-offs and welcome diverse perspectives to shape outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: When people are trusted with real questions and agency, we believe the proposals that emerge are stronger, and so is the relationship between citizen and state.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: While the Government has traditionally led in these areas, this has started to change in recent years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: PUB's Our Coastal Conversations is an example where the public discussed how we can protect our land against rising sea levels.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: At a session for City-East Coast, we listened to participants, whose views shaped our recommendations for Changi Beach Park.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We also agree with Mr Foo that citizen engagement should be at the heart of infrastructure planning and are learning from ground-up trials.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Today, HBD and Town Councils already engage residents on neighbourhood upgrades.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We will learn from these pilots to improve citizen involvement in the NRP consultation process.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Likewise, we are open to resident-led efforts that strengthen our recycling ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: For example, MSE is partnering Zero Waste SG's trial of dedicated recycling bins for clean stream recyclables in Pioneer.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We are encouraged that Mr Foo's residents have seen early success with their own collection drives and are looking forward to learning from their efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Mr Foo also suggested an approach centred on social impact and ground-up proposals for state properties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Social and community value are already key considerations in how state properties are allocated.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: SLA will continue to engage social startups and non-government organisations to understand their needs, and work with agencies to unlock more state properties with social impact.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Beyond these areas, the spirit of collaboration is just as vital, if not more so, for the next generation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: When you give young people a real responsibility, they rise to meet it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We will launch the next run of Youth Panels later this year for more youths to step forward and contribute.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The goal here is not consultation for its own sake.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: It is a government and its people thinking through hard problems side by side and arriving at better answers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: That is the ideal we are holding ourselves to and will continue creating opportunities to do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Volunteerism is citizenship in action and that instinct is alive and well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Many Singaporeans want to give their time and their skills to causes they believe in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Here, our role is to strengthen the conditions to help it to flourish.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We have learned that to sustain it, people need clear pathways to match their causes to their strengths and the assurance that their contributions make a difference.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We have been working hard to strengthen the volunteering ecosystem to make it more easy for Singaporeans to step forward and more meaningful for them to stay on.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Our island-wide network of 24 SG Cares Volunteer Centres works with community partners to identify town-level needs, such as senior befriending, and reaches out to interested citizens in areas to meet those needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: For our youths, Youth Corps Singapore has been championing youth volunteerism by bringing together youths to do good – and many of them are already doing so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Regardless of age, a giving society is one where people feel connected to something that is larger than themselves.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We want every Singaporean who steps forward to find exactly that.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The third front is when Singaporeans take it upon themselves to build what their communities need, ahead of any policies or programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: For these efforts to thrive, Government plays the role of enabler and partner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: That means providing funding that is accessible, processes that are responsive and a willingness to hold space and follow the lead of citizens who are closest to the opportunity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The residents of Tanjong Pagar group representative constituency are a great example of this – no one understands the community better than the very people who live in it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Our young people are perhaps most willing to simply start; to see something their community needs and build it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Earlier this year, I also announced that we will launch the Somerset Belt Youth CoLab.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: They are now working with youth communities to plan for the upcoming Youth Month in July.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: All that I have shared are proof of what is possible when Singaporeans step forward.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We want to make it easier for more of this to happen.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: For starters, we formed the SGPO as the first stop for any citizen who wants to partner the Government.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Anyone can submit your ideas through the Partners Portal.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: SGPO will open doors to the right partners – providing support from venues to volunteers and publicity – to bring your ideas to life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: If your idea is not fully formed, SGPO's Citizens' Circles will offer a safe space for you to refine your ideas with agencies and fellow citizens.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Ultimately, the most enduring community efforts are those that belong to people who built them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We want to give those efforts the best possible start and will refine our measures to keep barriers low and support relevant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: That partnering citizens well is a capability the Government must build with intention.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We are investing in structures, skills and the culture to engage citizens meaningfully.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The formation of the SGPO I mentioned earlier is a signal of that commitment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: MCCY has been facilitating the building of engagement capabilities across Government, and at all levels.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We are training our officers and our leaders, sharing best practices, and providing more opportunities for ground learning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Our goal is to rally agencies to step forward and work closely with our citizens across all three fronts that I spoke about today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We will continue pressing on to build a Public Service that is ready to partner citizens sincerely and wholeheartedly – and become better partners that our citizens can count on.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: He has reminded us that when Government and people lean in jointly, the whole is far greater than the sum of its parts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: That instinct and belief that we are stronger together is one of Singapore's greatest strengths, and it is one we must never take for granted.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: A democracy of deeds is something we build iteratively – learning as we go and always searching for a deeper partnership with our people.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: That is the work ahead and we take it on with conviction.
